To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
computer-extracted image texture features were associated with the error-making patterns of radiology residents in detecting mammographic masses.

the use of computer-extracted image feature information improves the performance of residents in detecting masses on screening mammograms and that the use of image feature information is most effective when the residents are presented with a limited number of features.
computer-extracted image texture and shape features can be used to distinguish between correct and incorrect responses to a mammographic mass detection task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computer-assisted system that will help radiologists in the detection of breast masses on mammograms.
the development of a new method for the automatic extraction of the shape of the mass in the image.
the development and validation of a new computer-assisted method for the detection of mammographic lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a computerized image feature extraction program can be useful in the training of radiology residents in the interpretation of mammographic masses.
, in general, the use of a computer-aided diagnosis system (CAD) in the interpretation of mammograms does not improve the diagnostic performance of radiologists and may even be detrimental.
the use of a computerized mammographic mass detection system can be used to help improve the detection of masses among radiology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel approach to model error-making patterns in radiology trainees by using computer-extracted image characteristics and a novel machine learning approach.
computer extracted image features can be used to model error making patterns in the detection of mammographic mass lesions.

the use of computer-extracted image characteristics in a model of error-making patterns for the detection of mammographic lesions among radiology residents is feasible and that the model is able to discriminate between residents who do and do not make a specific type of mistake (false-negative errors).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of radiology residents can be predicted using image features extracted by computer.
we have developed a new approach for modeling of error making patterns in mammographic interpretation.
